questionText:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

The massive exterior wall of the old mansion was being painted by the skilled laborers when it suddenly started raining heavily.

options.A: The skilled laborers had been painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.B: The skilled laborers are painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.C: The skilled laborers were painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.D: The skilled laborers painted the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.a: The skilled laborers had been painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.b: The skilled laborers are painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.c: The skilled laborers were painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.
options.d: The skilled laborers painted the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily.

solution:
Rule: The past continuous passive ('was being painted') converts to the past continuous active ('were painting'). The agent becomes the subject.

The passive sentence "The massive exterior wall... was being painted by the skilled laborers..." is in the past continuous tense. To convert to active, the agent 'the skilled laborers' becomes the subject. The verb phrase 'was being painted' changes to 'were painting'.

Option 1 uses the past perfect continuous, changing the tense. Option 2 mixes present and past tenses. Option 3 uses the simple past, losing the continuous aspect.

Correct Answer is The skilled laborers were painting the massive exterior wall of the old mansion when it suddenly started raining heavily because it correctly uses the active past continuous tense.
conceptTested: Conversion of past continuous passive tense ('was being painted') to past continuous active tense ('were painting').

options.d: Several items destroyed in the room by the burglar. Even the carpet he has torn.

solution:
Rule: The simple past active voice ('destroyed') converts to the simple past passive voice ('were destroyed'). The present perfect passive ('has been torn') remains as is.

The active sentence "The burglar destroyed several items..." is in the simple past tense. To convert to passive, the object 'several items' becomes the subject. The verb 'destroyed' changes to 'were destroyed'. The second sentence is already in passive and should remain unchanged.

Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Let the documents be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.

options.A: You should submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
options.B: Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
options.C: The documents will be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.

options.c: The documents will be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.
options.d: Let the head of the department submit the documents by the end of the week.

solution:
Rule: For a passive imperative sentence starting with 'Let', the active voice is formed by directly starting with the base form of the verb.

The passive imperative "Let the documents be submitted..." instructs that an action be done. To convert to active, the instruction is given directly: "Submit the documents...". The 'Let' and 'be' are removed, and the verb takes its base form.

Option 1 is a suggestion, not a command. Option 3 changes the tense. Option 4 is a suggestion to another person.

Correct Answer is Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week because it correctly converts the passive imperative to an active command.

questionText:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

People eat rice in many countries.

options.A: Rice was eaten by people in many countries.
options.B: Rice was eaten in many countries.
options.C: Rice is eaten in many countries.
options.D: Rice has been eaten by people in many countries.
options.a: Rice was eaten by people in many countries.
options.b: Rice was eaten in many countries.
options.c: Rice is eaten in many countries.
options.d: Rice has been eaten by people in many countries.

solution:
Rule: The simple present active voice ('eat') converts to the simple present passive voice ('is eaten'). When the subject is general (e.g., 'people'), the agent phrase is often omitted.

The active sentence "People eat rice in many countries" is in the simple present tense. To convert to passive, the object 'rice' becomes the subject. The verb 'eat' changes to 'is eaten'. Since 'people' is a general subject, the agent 'by people' is usually omitted.

Option 1 uses the simple past. Option 2 omits the verb 'is'. Option 4 uses the present perfect.

Correct Answer is Rice is eaten in many countries because it correctly uses the simple present passive and omits the unnecessary agent.
conceptTested: Conversion of simple present active voice to simple present passive voice with omission of general agents.
